minimum_window.why: User decisions: smallest supported device 1366x768; window not shrinkable below 1280x720 logical; right-dock threshold delegated to the agent ('sao cho hop ly la duoc').

decisions.window_minimum: startup::effective_min_size: per axis max(800x400 floor, min(1280x720, monitor_logical - (16,80))); unknown monitor -> 1280x720. Builder gets the floor 800x400; MatrixApp::show sends ViewportCommand::MinInnerSize on frame 0 and on change. AppConfig.min_window nominal 1280x720 (start below it refused).
decisions.high_dpi_conflict: 1366x768 at 125%/150% is 1093x614 / 911x512 logical; a hard 1280x720 cannot fit, so the minimum is capped to the usable area: 1366x768@100% -> 1280x688, @125% -> 1076.8x534.4, @150% -> 894.7x432. Work area is ESTIMATED (egui/winit do not expose it; Win32 would need unsafe/FFI). Reserve includes the title bar (one constant SHELL_RESERVE_PT; taskbar-only is a user choice).
decisions.planner_floor: PLAN_FLOOR_WINDOW 800x400 replaces 560x286 (320x286 without rail); rail-independent. Behaviour below the floor unchanged (WindowTooSmall, Layout: error, last good plan). NotEnoughRoom and LeftRailShrunk unreachable, variants kept.
decisions.right_dock_threshold: NARROW_WINDOW_WIDTH 900 -> 1200 logical points. Viewport width (W-602)/2 is 299 pt at 1200 vs 156.5 pt at the old 915.

notes: Real window: the harness itself was broken by the 2026-10-17 tree merge (it looked for <root>/target/debug/om9.exe while the build uses CARGO_TARGET_DIR, and it ran the app with cwd=<root>/standalone, which no longer exists). Both are fixed in tools/validate_m01_l3_003_panels.py. After the fix it runs 6/7 PASS; the one failure is `readback-recover` (extra float_after_readback.3 132.0 != 120.0, notes [] lack Recovered) — a FLOATING PANE MINIMUM case, not the Object Info label, and NOT diagnosed yet. The panel scenarios do not select an object, so they cannot prove the label: a scripted selection scenario is the next slice. No real-window claim is made for the label.

RESOLVED AND GREEN: the harness expectation was stale and is corrected. The scenario now forces the window-readback path with a 300x40 rectangle; the app clamps it to [28,49,300,120] (FLOAT_MIN_HEIGHT) and says 'Display was moved back inside the window'; one frame later the REAL window reports its own 132 px height, above the minimum and inside the work area, which the readback legitimately accepts. The harness asserts on the forced clamp and the message (float_after_force.2/3, message_after_force) instead of the frame-later state. Full harness: 7/7 PASS.

Window harness: 7/7 PASS (verified twice; one earlier 'float-drop exit -1' was a race with a concurrent cargo build, not a code regression — run alone it passes). The Object Info label still has no window photo. Findings for the next attempt: (1) OM9_UI_AUDIT_PANELS is validated against PANEL_AUDIT_SCENARIOS in ui.rs, so a new scenario needs its name added there (this was the real cause of the three timeouts); (2) record_panel_checks DOES fill left_order, work_area, floating and drag_in_progress from live state, so a receipt whose checks lack those fields did not come from the arm we added — verify the dispatch actually takes it (log audit.panel_checks.len()) before trusting the run.

REAL WINDOW: the new `object-info` audit scenario drew one line, selected it and the receipt carries dock.object_info = {"kind": "Line", "label": "Line \u00b7 10.000 \u00d7 4.000 \u00d7 0.000 \u00b7 valid"}; the screenshot is implementation/evidence/M01/OM9-L3-03-14-005/object-info-label-in-a-real-window.png. The scenario passes on its own (3 consecutive runs) and in a full run was once killed by the OS (exit -1, no receipt) — a harness-level transient already seen with float-drop; a one-retry in tools/validate_m01_l3_003_panels.py is the next small fix. Two real causes found on the way: the scenario name had to be added to PANEL_AUDIT_SCENARIOS (ui.rs) and the dispatch arm needed `return` (without it the default drag script ran too).

FINAL: the real-window harness has EIGHT scenarios now (the seventh was object-info) and passes 8/8; the single verification point tools/verify_m01_l2_03_14.py is 13/13 groups ok (exit 0), saved as implementation/evidence/M01/OM9-L2-03-14/AUTOMATED_VERIFICATION.log. Fixes that made it stable: the scenario name in PANEL_AUDIT_SCENARIOS, the missing `return` in the dispatch arm, a repaint until the shot is requested (otherwise the window idles before the record step), the focus step waiting for the status row (roll-up's intermittent lost first click), a one-retry for a killed launch, and the harness picking the check entry by scenario name.
